tier_reason: PR #26 (jkbonfield, opened 2021-06-17, merged 2022-04-12) gives first-party encode/decode MB/s tables on a named CPU (Xeon Gold 6142) with an FSE order-0 row as an external baseline, but compiler flags are not stated (only 'Ubuntu 18.04 system gcc'), so not A; no independent measurement.

corrections.baseline: Scalar 4-way rANS4x16 codec in the same library (r4x16 -o0) and FSE order-0 (tANS), both rows on the PR's tables
corrections.claimed_speedup: PR #26, high-complexity HiSeq quals (101 MB), Xeon Gold 6142, MB/s encode/decode: FSE order-0 416.3/564.4; r4x16 -o0 (4-way) 428.8/773.9; 32x16 (-o4) scalar 358.8/642.4, SSE4 360.9/954.0, AVX2 578.7/1516.0, AVX512 809.9/2124.8. AVX512 decode is about 2.7x r4x16 -o0 and 3.8x FSE (derived from page data); SSE4/scalar 32-way encode is slower than 4-way. Graviton-2 order-0: 4x16 -o0 347.6/452.6, 32x16 scalar 343.8/437.3, NEON 365.4/736.2.
corrections.compiler_and_flags: Ubuntu 18.04 system gcc (PR comment: gcc-7.5.0; gcc-11 encode 268.2 MB/s versus gcc-7 431.5 MB/s; clang-10 393.7 enc / 827.3 dec MB/s); optimisation flags not stated
corrections.caveats: Numbers are first-party from a 2021 pull-request description (merged April 2022); hardware named, flags not stated. The repo also carries BENCHMARKS.md, a maintained snapshot on the same Xeon Gold 6142 (10 MB NovaSeq quals: r4x16-o0 400.3/716.1 MB/s versus r32x16-o4 AVX512 866.9/2098.6 MB/s) that compares only internal codecs plus fqzcomp and bsc. The 32-way scalar and SSE4 encoders are slower than the 4-way codec; gains are mainly in decode and with AVX2/AVX512. LICENSE.md is BSD (3-clause style, Genome Research Ltd) with listed files (c_range_coder.h, rANS_byte.h, rANS_word.h, ...) public domain/CC0 (no patent grant for those).

notes: Record's 'decode 773.9 (4x16 scalar)' is the 4-way -o0 codec, not the 32-way scalar (642.4); Graviton 'NEON 437 to 736' conflated the 32x16 scalar row (437.3) with the 4x16 baseline (452.6), corrected. Last commit 2026-09-24 ('Make all inputs constant (#152)') and 40 stars confirmed.

tier_reason: README tables give first-party decode throughput on a named CPU (Ryzen 9 7950X) against FSE, FSE Huff0 and htscodecs; build files (project.lua: -O3, LTO for Linux ReleaseClang) are public, but the clang version is not stated and the README does not show that the baselines ran through the repo's own harness (TurboANX came from a separate TurboBench run), so not A.

corrections.compiler_and_flags: clang++ (version not stated); project.lua sets -O3, -mxsave and LinkTimeOptimization for the Linux ReleaseClang config (premake5 gmake2, config=releaseclang_x64)
corrections.caveats: Ratio and speed trade-offs are per variant; the headline 'raw' row has slightly worse ratio (64.48 % versus FSE 63.2 % and Huff0 63.4 %). Win is decode only: the top row encodes at 336.81 MiB/s versus FSE 736.10 and Huff0 1,581.32 MiB/s; README says all encoders are scalar and not particularly optimized, and the best decoders require AVX2. TurboANX (closed source) is within about 2% (2,964.02 versus 3,018.02 MiB/s) and comes from a June 2023 TurboBench run on a native Windows build, so mixed environment. Compiler version not stated. First-party benchmark. The author calls it an R&D repo not yet finalized for integration. README also lists multithreaded variants up to 18,035.77 MiB/s decode. Last commit is a dependabot actions bump (2024-09-03).

notes: enwik8 rows (3,018.02 / 966.58 / 2,515.23 / 2,374.04 MiB/s), hardware and 'up to 3.3 GB/s' all confirmed on the README; BSD-2-Clause and 21 stars confirmed. github.io graph page not opened (blocked host).

tier_reason: README shows first-party clocks/symbol and MiB/s on a Sandy Bridge i7-2600K for scalar versus interleaved versus 8-way SSE 4.1 decode; example programs are public but compiler and flags are not stated and the author says the measurement setup is not great.

corrections.claimed_speedup: book1, i7-2600K, decode: rans_byte scalar 22.0-23.5 clocks/symbol (137.5-147.1 MiB/s) versus 2-way interleaved 13.7-14.2 (227.2-236.2 MB/s); rans64 scalar 18.5-19.6 (165.0-174.6 MiB/s) versus interleaved 10.6-11.2 (287.7-305.7 MB/s); rans_word_sse41 8-way decode 5.9-6.2 clocks/symbol (520.1-550.8 MB/s). The SIMD decoder is roughly 3.7x rans_byte scalar decode (derived from page data).

notes: Numbers confirmed in README (rans64 interleaved range extends to 10.6 clocks / 305.7 MB/s, corrected). Public domain (CC0, 'Clarify public domain license'), 371 stars, last commit 2018-11-25 confirmed; baseline is only the author's own scalar rANS, which is a weak but named comparison for a widely referenced reference implementation.
